_comment: Keyframed offsets for the first-person hands. Read by BOTH packages/core/src/modules/hassault/viewclips.ts and apps/native-fps/src/viewclips.rs (include_str!), and pinned together by apps/native-fps/tests/browser_parity.rs — two hand-typed copies of forty keyframes drift on the very first tweak. Every pose is an OFFSET from the weapon's grip anchor (models/grips.json), in the weapon's own space, so a keyframe that names no channel leaves that hand on the gun. That is what makes a partial track legal, and it is what makes the two layers composable at all. `t` is normalised 0..1 over the clip's own length, never seconds: the reload track then stretches to whatever reloadTime the server served, so a 1.4s pistol and a 2.6s shotgun share one authored motion.

locomotion._comment: The base layer. Looping, phase-driven off the view model's own bobPhase so it can never drift out of step with the bob. t=0 and t=1 must be identical or the cycle ticks once per stride.

actions._comment: The upper layer. One-shot, and it REPLACES the channels it names rather than blending with locomotion — models/clips.ts already explains that two poses averaged on one bone give you half a reload, and makes its track sets disjoint for exactly this reason.

reload._comment: Off the handguard, down to the magazine well.
Charging handle — the primary hand comes off the grip for a moment, which is the beat that makes a reload read as mechanical rather than as a dip.

throw._comment: Pull the pin: the support hand comes across to the primary.
Windup, back and up over the shoulder.
